comment: Agree on the agent, disagree on the lane. The patient is oxaliplatin-naive after adjuvant FOLFIRI, the preference set says treat to remission with efficacy weight 0.80 and accept high-risk-high-reward, and RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) is the combo platform that turns the 35% pooled-G12X ORR into something with a deeper-response ceiling. Picking monotherapy on a no-veto patient who has explicitly invited the trade reads as conservative-frame leakage past the preference field.

The ROBINS-I Moderate framing on RMC-6236-001 is technically right and operationally wrong for a 2L PDAC patient with no RCT-grade options on her allele. The same evidence frame relegates RMC-7977 + ivonescimab (Wasko Nature 2024, pmid:38588697) to no-rank, but the autochthonous KPC complete-response data are the strongest preclinical PDAC effect size in the dossier and deserved at least a watch slot rather than a clean exclusion. Pure RoB hierarchy under-weights mechanism in a setting where the registrational trial has not read out and the patient is moving now.

Targeting the rank-2 pick because the gating is harsher than the row admits. Olaparib at rank 2 requires both a germline BRCA / PALB2 hit that is not on file and a 16-plus-week platinum induction the patient has never had — that is two sequential bets stacked against a tumor that is already recurrent. Ranking it ahead of an MTAP-cooperative or PD-1 x VEGF combination lane misreads the time budget for a patient whose stated goal is remission, and the POLO interim OS HR 0.91 (pmid:31157963) means even when the gates open the payoff is PFS, not OS.

The advocate row reads the preferences correctly and then ranks against them. Free-text says treat to remission, accept high-risk-high-reward, efficacy weight 0.80, oxaliplatin-naive — that is the exact profile for putting RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) chemo-combo at rank 1 and monotherapy NCT05379985 at rank 2, not the reverse. The Wolpin 2026 monotherapy ORR 35% / mPFS 8.5 is the floor of what this allele can do on this drug; the combo backbone is where the depth-of-response upside lives.

Stacking pan-RAS-class rash and GI toxicity onto PD-1xVEGF-class immune-mediated AEs in a regimen with zero published PDAC clinical safety data is the exact scenario the conservative axis flags. RMC-7977 + ivonescimab has no dedicated combination-tolerability publication, no PDAC-cohort AE distribution, and no management algorithm for overlapping rash-versus-immune-rash diagnostic ambiguity. Preferences.json lists no formal vetoes so this is dissent rather than veto, but the missing datum is the combined G3+ AE distribution at the proposed RP2D.

Daraxonrasib monotherapy at 300 mg has a mapped AE profile (G3+ ~30%, rash 91% / G3+ 8%, diarrhea 48% / G3+ 2%, stomatitis 31% / G3+ 3%) and I concur on the monotherapy rank-1. The rank-2 RMC-GI-102 chemo-combo carries the qualifier: pan-RAS plus mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab has no published dedicated combination-safety readout in PDAC yet, and residual neuropathy from prior FOLFIRI compounds the oxaliplatin watch-item. Treat the chemo-combo arm as a contingent escalation pending public release of the RMC-GI-102 PDAC-cohort AE distribution.

POLO is the only RoB2-low RCT in this dossier and the only PARP-class regimen with seven years of post-marketing surveillance in PDAC. The two gating workups (germline BRCA / PALB2 panel, platinum induction) sit upstream of any clinical decision, so this is a deferred option rather than an active one — but the evidence-quality ranking is correct and the load-bearing PFS HR 0.53 holds.

ELI-002 has the cleanest published safety profile in the dossier (no DLTs, no G3+ vaccine-attributed events across AMPLIFY-201 n=25) so toxicity is not the issue. The qualifier is that the patient is overt-recurrent and AMPLIFY-7P enrolls MRD-positive resected disease; the NCCN v2.2026 trial-enrollment principle does not bridge a clinically distinct subpopulation. Trial is active not recruiting per registry, which collapses the question to academic.

The 5-of-6 figure at dose level 1 is an ASCO 2024 abstract (DOI 10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.4140) with no peer-reviewed publication, ROBINS-I:Serious, and n=6 at the relevant dose; an exact binomial 95% CI on 5/6 runs roughly 36 to 100 percent, and a single non-responder collapses the point estimate. Anchoring an access-pursuit on a six-patient signal in an abstract that has not cleared peer review is the small-N regression-to-the-mean trap. The LGSOC readout (PMID 40644648) is cross-tumor and adds a four-agent stack (RAF/MEK clamp + FAKi + gem/nab) whose combination toxicity envelope in PDAC has no published characterization.

Preference fit is real but the evidence base for RMC-7977 plus ivonescimab in PDAC is zero published clinical data; the rank-3 rationale rests on a KPC GEMM paper (PMID 38588697) and a G12R microenvironment-distinctiveness inference (PMID 38589574). Preclinical activity in a G12D autochthonous model is not allele-matched to G12R and does not substitute for indication data. Layering pan-RAS class toxicity (rash 91 percent any-grade, diarrhea 48 percent from the daraxonrasib record at PMID 42090791) on top of a PD-1xVEGF bispecific without a published PDAC combination-safety dataset is the specific gap to flag before this becomes an option the patient is asked to choose.

The NCCN trial-enrollment principle is a procedural recommendation, not a drug-level category 1 or 2A endorsement of daraxonrasib, and the concensusite framing should not borrow guideline weight that the agent itself has not earned. RASolute 302 (NCT06625320) is active-not-recruiting with no OS readout on file; the load-bearing efficacy datum remains Wolpin NEJM 2026 (PMID 42090791) at n=26 in 2L RAS G12 with no allele-resolved G12R subgroup, ROBINS-I:Moderate. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation is a regulatory process status, not confirmation of effect. Call this what it is: a guideline-aligned trial-enrollment option, not a guideline-endorsed regimen.

Reiss 2021 (PMID 33970687) is single-arm phase 2 at n=46 with PFS rate at 6 months as the registered primary endpoint; the mPFS 13.1 and mOS 23.5 figures are responder-enriched secondary readouts in a platinum-sensitive cohort and carry nothing like the registrational weight of POLO. ROBINS-I:Moderate, no concurrent comparator, sponsor analysis. The toxicity profile is well-characterized as a PARP class effect, which earns the rank-4 placement, but the rationale quotes the secondary efficacy numbers with more confidence than an n=46 single-arm design supports. Both the germline gate and the absent platinum induction remain the binding constraints either way.

RMC-7977 + ivonescimab sits two pre-approval layers off the NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 menu: pan-RAS(ON) has no PDAC category listing, and the PD-1xVEGF bispecific is not in any NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO PDAC line. The preclinical KPC anchor (pmid:38588697) is G12D in an autochthonous mouse model with no clinical PDAC readout, and the listed cohorts on NCT07397338 are NSCLC and CRC. The NCCN trial-enrollment principle can cover the daraxonrasib lane without forcing the board onto an unproven two-axis stack that no society has scored.

Agree daraxonrasib belongs at rank 1, and agree the agent itself has not yet earned a NCCN drug-level category — that is exactly the framing in concensusite rank-1 already. The qualifier on the critic row is that the n=26 single-arm with no comparator framing understates the collective calibration that has already happened around the same data: FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and the NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 trial-enrollment principle are the field reading the Wolpin NEJM 2026 cohort (pmid:42090791) as enrollment-worthy for an actionable KRAS alteration despite the absence of phase 3 OS. ROBINS-I scoring is a fine internal exercise; it does not displace the consensus route the guideline already names.

ELI-002 7P has the cleanest safety read in the dossier, but AMPLIFY-7P (NCT05726864) enrolls MRD-positive resected disease and this patient has overt recurrent disease; the indication is off, not just borderline. NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 lists no KRAS vaccine in any category, and the trial-enrollment principle does not stretch to a trial whose entry criteria explicitly exclude the patient's setting. Safety profile is not a substitute for an open eligibility window.

Rank-1 daraxonrasib monotherapy on NCT05379985 lines up with the NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 trial-enrollment principle and is fine as written. Rank-2 daraxonrasib + mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab on NCT06445062 stacks an unlisted pan-RAS agent onto a NCCN cat-1 chemo backbone with no published combination-safety data, which is a step further off the guideline than the mono lane and should be flagged as such when discussed with the patient. The treat-to-remission preference is real, but the combo route's guideline-fit is weaker than the rationale presents.

Risktaker's rank 1 lands on the same recruiting trial the preference set points at, and the chemo-combo variant on NCT06445062 reads the patient's treat-to-remission goal and accept-high-risk-high-reward clause at face value rather than discounting them. Oxaliplatin-naive status is the operational reason a deeper-cytoreduction arm is actually available, which matters when the 0.80 efficacy weight is doing the ranking. No toxicity-veto conflict to flag because preferences.json carries no formal vetoes, and the rash / GI class effects sit inside the consent envelope this patient already signed.

The RCT-grade-evidence case for ranking olaparib above the recruiting pan-KRAS phase 1 is internally clean, but it cuts against prefers_trials=true and the treat-to-remission goal when two gates are still locked — the germline panel has not returned and the patient is platinum-naive after irinotecan-only adjuvant FOLFIRI. POLO's interim OS HR of 0.91 softens the case for paying the 16-week induction tax before the maintenance pathway even opens. If germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 comes back positive on the workup the rank climbs; until then the preference set reads this as a parked option, not an active rank 2.

POLO is the only NCCN category 1 listing on this board, so the guideline-fit logic for putting olaparib above PF-07934040 is honest. The preference-fit case tilts the other way: olaparib needs a germline-positive result plus a fresh platinum induction plus 16 weeks of disease control before it is even operative, and the patient asked for trials and remission-directed treatment at an efficacy weight of 0.80. Guideline-fit and preference-fit pull opposite directions here and the preference-fit voice is the louder one for this patient. Worth keeping in pocket if the germline reflex returns BRCA1/2 or PALB2.

Conservative's rank 1 is the daraxonrasib monotherapy lane on NCT05379985, the same trial and agent the preference set points at, and the rash / GI / stomatitis profile has routine management algorithms with no toxicity-veto conflict because preferences.json carries no formal vetoes. The one advocate-side note is that stepping away from the RMC-GI-102 chemo-combo arm leaves some of the deeper-cytoreduction potential the treat-to-remission goal points at on the table, but the combination-safety dataset is genuinely thinner so the rank-1 call holds on its own terms. The downstream olaparib pick carries the same germline-and-platinum gating issue noted on the critic and concensusite rows.
